title: Country risk classification
min_scope: Commission benchmarking classification (low/standard/high) under Art. 29 and the due diligence level it triggers. Sources: Reg. (EU) 2023/1115; Impl. Reg. (EU) 2025/1093; Reg. (EU) 2025/2650.

title: Presence of forests
min_scope: Forest cover, primary forest, peatland presence in sourcing areas.

title: Indigenous peoples & customary tenure
min_scope: Presence of indigenous peoples in production areas; FPIC legal baseline; consultation in good faith; documented claims/unrest; active grievances from credible sources.

title: Prevalence of deforestation
min_scope: Tree cover loss trend, state of primary forest, loss in protected areas, agriculture-driven loss, post-2020 trend.

title: Governance concerns
min_scope: Corruption (TI CPI), palm sector regulation quality, EU/UN sanctions, civic space (CIVICUS), transparency indices, tracked environmental crimes.

title: Supply chain complexity
min_scope: Palm supply chain structure: planted area, mills, refineries, kernel crushers, biodiesel plants; smallholder share; independent vs linked plantations; traceability implications.

title: Risk of mixing
min_scope: Entry points for unknown-origin material: dealers/collection points, mill weighbridges, multi-origin refinery blending, bulk port tanks, cross-border flows; certification model limits (MB vs SG/IP). Synthesis section: must reference S4-S6 findings.

title: Human rights
min_scope: Labour/human rights law enforcement: forced and child labour listings, import control measures (e.g. CBP WROs), migrant workforce structure, recruitment practices, national action plans.

title: Substantiated concerns
min_scope: First-party grievances and coalition submissions alleging non-compliance for palm products from the country/region. Synthesis section: must reference grievance data and quantitative findings.

title: Certification & third-party schemes
min_scope: Coverage and content of mandatory and voluntary schemes (e.g. MSPO, ISPO, RSPO; MB/SG/IP models) against Art. 9 information requirements. Certification is supportive evidence, never a green lane.
